In response to the recent protests, Ibiza Island Council President Vicent Marí said the island has been a "pioneer" in combating tourist overcrowding, according to Cadena SER.

The Ibiza demonstration comes amid broader tensions surrounding mass tourism across Spain.

In recent years, Barcelona residents have taken to the streets to protest mass tourism, with some demonstrators spraying visitors with water guns.

On Mallorca, another of Spain's Balearic Islands, viral videos showed pickpockets targeting tourists near the island's capital of Palma.

item.title: How Charlie Kirk inspired his mentor's fight to defend reality
item.description: Frank Turek stood feet away when Charlie Kirk was fatally shot at Utah Valley University. Now his new book carries on Kirk's apologetics mission.
item.content:encoded:
For decades, author Frank Turek has defended the idea that a Christian worldview offers the truest explanation of reality. The murder of his close friend, Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk one year ago, only reinforced that conviction.

Now, Turek is sharing those beliefs in his new book, "The War on Reality: Recovering Truth in a World that Celebrates Lies," co-authored with Phoenix Hayes. The book argues that popular culture views about the family, gender, education and politics defy logic and aims to equip Christians to challenge these beliefs.

Kirk's wife, Erika, wrote the foreword for the book, in which Turek says she reveals the source of her late husband's quiet confidence during hostile debates on college campuses.

BENNY JOHNSON RECALLS HOW CHARLIE KIRK HELPED HIS FAMILY AFTER ARSON DESTROYED THEIR DC HOME

"She writes that the reason Charlie would go to college campuses and not get flustered is because he knew that the foundation of his belief was true — that there is a God, he is not Him," Turek told Fox News Digital. 

"He has put us on this earth to know him and to make him known through Jesus," Turek said. "And everything else is really just details. And so he could stand firm on a college campus despite any kind of threat or despite any question that might come his way. But he knew he had to be prepared to answer those questions."

As an example of this "war on reality," Turek pointed to the debate over transgender issues, which he argued has caused immeasurable harm to women and children.

"It's a contradictory worldview that tragically is hurting children the most, because we have people now, politicians and mostly Democrats saying... what we ought to do is transition children that are confused about their sexuality," Turek said. "This is not care, this is child abuse. It's a war on women, by the way, because now women aren't protected in women's sports or in women's changing facilities."

Turek mentored Kirk on applying strategies he discusses in the book, such as employing the laws of logic and identifying fallacies when responding to polarizing cultural topics. 

Their friendship began in 2020 after Kirk asked Turek to mentor him in Christian apologetics, which is the practice of defending Christianity with evidence and reasoning. Turek said their bond deepened over time until he came to view Kirk as a son.

BILL MAHER TO APPEAR IN CHARLIE KIRK DOCUMENTARY, REMEMBERS LOVING HIS INTERVIEW WITH THE TPUSA LEADER

"Charlie was the same person offstage that he was onstage. He was somebody that was always trying to learn," Turek told Fox News Digital. "It can be hard to mentor somebody smarter than you, but not with Charlie, because the only thing that exceeded his intellect was his humility. The few things that I knew that he wanted to know, he asked me to tell him. So we would get together and discuss questions he might get on a college campus, because I've been presenting on college campuses for about 20 years. And we would sharpen one another."

Turek was standing just feet away when Kirk was shot and killed Sept. 10 at Utah Valley University during the first stop of TPUSA’s "The American Comeback Tour."

At Kirk's memorial service weeks later, Turek reflected on his friend's faith.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"Now, I want you to know that Charlie, right now, is in heaven," Turek said at the service. "Not because he was a great husband and father, not because he saved millions of kids out of darkness on college campuses, not because he changed minds and chased votes to save the country, not because he sacrificed himself for his Savior. Charlie Kirk is in heaven because his Savior sacrificed himself for Charlie Kirk."

Ultimately, Turek hopes his book encourages Christians and churches to speak out boldly in the public square and to carry on Kirk's legacy.

"I hear from pastors all the time, 'I don't get involved in politics, I just preach the gospel,' to which I say to them, 'I guess you don't think the gospel is very important then.' And they say, 'Well, what do you mean?' And I say, 'Because the laws that are made politically can affect your ability to preach and live the gospel'... So for no other reason, Christians have to be involved in politics to protect our ability to preach and live the gospel, to have religious freedom," Turek said. 

"The second reason, major reason, is because we're called to love one another. And God set up governments to protect innocent people from evil. According to Romans 13, the government is supposed to punish wrongdoers. Why will we not put laws in place as Christians to punish people who are doing evil? We should," Turek said.

item.title: Mysterious settlement discovered after residents seemingly packed up and vanished
item.description: A medieval village near Halberstadt in Saxony-Anhalt was abandoned in a "highly orderly fashion," archaeologists say — but why the residents left remains a mystery.
item.content:encoded:
Archaeologists recently uncovered the remains of a medieval village that was mysteriously abandoned in Germany — raising questions about why its residents packed up and left.

The excavation at the Am Frevelgraben site in Halberstadt, in the German state of Saxony-Anhalt, revealed numerous traces of a medieval settlement, including parts of a multi-tiered ditch system.

The State Office for Monument Preservation and Archaeology Saxony-Anhalt announced the findings on Aug. 24.

UNEXPECTED ANCIENT COMPLEX EMERGES NEAR BIBLICAL CITY LINKED TO JONAH AND ST PETER

Archaeologists began excavating the site in March ahead of the development of a nearby industrial park, officials said. 

Historical maps suggest the settlement may be the remains of a medieval village known as Kühlingen.

Archaeologists documented rows of pit houses, settlement pits and two wells at the site, while other traces suggest residents also made extensive use of the nearby riverbank.

Overlapping features and houses built directly next to one another indicate the settlement developed in two phases, officials said — with its footprint shifting as new homes were constructed.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER 1,700-YEAR-OLD CHRISTIAN CITY HIDDEN BENEATH EGYPT'S DESERT

Despite the well-preserved remains, however, archaeologists found surprisingly few artifacts — a detail officials found remarkable.

"A few scattered ceramic shards and a handful of metal finds, including, for example, a bronze tap, fittings, and belt buckets, certainly represent only a fraction of the former possessions of the inhabitants," the release said.

The settlement was abandoned "in a highly orderly fashion," Oliver Dietrich, a spokesperson for the State Office for Heritage Management and Archaeology Saxony-Anhalt, told Fox News Digital.

"It was indeed striking how few artifacts were left behind," he said. "Medieval deserted villages typically yield a wealth of artifacts."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Dietrich said archaeologists found no evidence of destruction or fire at the site, and said the reason behind the abandonment "remains a mystery at this time."

"Further analysis will produce further insights into the abandonment process," he said.

The settlement is "clearly medieval," though researchers are not sure precisely when it was abandoned, Dietrich added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"Because of the scarcity of finds, radiocarbon analyses of selected animal bones are expected to provide a precise date," he said.

As fascinating as it is, the expert added that Am Frevelgraben is one of hundreds of deserted medieval villages in Germany.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"The most drastic period of abandonment was during the 14th and 15th centuries," Dietrich said, citing the Black Death, migration and climate change.

Often these villages "had too few resources to sustain the people," he said.

The find follows a similar discovery made recently in neighboring Poland.

Earlier this year, archaeologists uncovered another abandoned medieval settlement, Stolzenberg, which had remained hidden in a remote forest for centuries.

item.title: Letitia James’ Times Square shooting probe draws GOP criticism over New York’s mental health crisis
item.description: Saritha Komatireddy proposes a new Office of Civil Commitment after the Times Square fatal stabbing, saying New York fails mentally ill people.
item.content:encoded:
New York Attorney General Letitia James is facing scrutiny after opening up a legally required investigation into the police shooting of a woman who fatally stabbed Erin Piacenti, Bank of America executive and a new mother in her first week back to work from maternity leave, in Times Square.

James' office announced on Wednesday that it will be investigating Pamela Cisneros' death, who was wielding two large knives in each hand when officers confronted her following the fatal stabbing. She was ordered to drop the weapons but did not comply and was shot when she moved toward the officers.

Under state law, the Attorney General's Office of Special Investigation is mandated to investigate all deaths that were caused by police officers. However, Republican attorney general candidate Saritha Komatireddy is pushing the Attorney General's Office to take more concrete steps to ensure that another tragic killing or attack caused by a mentally unstable person doesn't happen again. She argued that an investigation into police conduct fails to address the real problem.

"The problem is that we have people who are known dangerous individuals, people with documented mental illness," Komatireddy told Fox News Digital. "They've been in the courts before, or they've been to the hospitals before. The police know exactly who they are, but we have no ability to take care of them."

REPUBLICANS GET 'AGGRESSIVE' IN FIGHT TO WIN TOP COP SPOTS IN BATTLEGROUND STATES

A campaign spokesperson for James accused Komatireddy of seeking to "score cheap political points off of a tragedy."

"Saritha Komatireddy wants to be Attorney General but doesn’t understand the law," a spokesperson said in an email to Fox News Digital. "Under New York’s Executive Law, the Office of the Attorney General’s Office of Special Investigation is required to investigate any incident where a police officer’s actions may have caused a death, including this one."

However, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who has a history of anti-police rhetoric, applauded the officers who stopped Cisneros.

"I want to thank the NYPD officers who stepped in and prevented a horrific attack from becoming even worse," Mamdani said at a news conference.

PARENTS IN BRONX NEIGHBORHOOD PLEAD FOR NYPD GUARD AS MAMDANI CUTS COPS, HALTS HIRES: 'HORRIBLE SITUATION'

New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch shared that while Cisneros, who lived in Queens, didn't have an arrest record in the city, there were two times police responded to calls concerning her suffering a mental health crisis.

In March 2019, Cisneros attempted suicide by jumping onto the tracks of the E train and was removed and later hospitalized. In March 2018, police found her in Midtown, where she was screaming, acting belligerent and intoxicated.

If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Under the state's Mental Hygiene Law, police and doctors can take a person to the hospital for a psychological hold if they are deemed to be a risk to themselves or others, or they can not meet their basic needs — but often times those with severe mental illnesses are released by the hospital back onto the streets hours after being brought in.

LETITIA JAMES FACES SCRUTINY AFTER NEW YORK CITY SPENDS $81,700 PER HOMELESS PERSON AMID SHELTER SCANDALS

"I was there in Times Square — just a couple of days after this fatal stabbing — and I was walking around and saw severely mentally ill people on the street," Komatireddy told Fox News Digital. "It's still happening every day, and we need someone who's actually going to propose a real solution and way forward."

TRUMP WANTS TO HELP 146,000 MENTALLY ILL WHO ARE HOMELESS. DEMOCRATS WANT TO STOP HIM

The New York State Office of Mental Health is tasked with overseeing the state's mental health system, which includes 23 psychiatric centers and 6,500 programs overseen by local governments and nonprofits. In addition, Komatireddy said that, if elected, she'd create a new office known as the Office of Civil Commitment that would target and keep tabs on people who are at most risk.

"The Office of Civil Commitment that I'm going to launch will be staffed with both law enforcement personnel and also physicians, and you need both because, under state law, the law requires that physicians certify that someone has the mental state required for involuntary civil commitment," Komatireddy told Fox News Digital. "So there's nothing like that right now in New York state. There's no office that has both law enforcement and physicians who can work together to get these people off the streets."

Greene County Sheriff Peter Kusminsky told Fox News Digital that his deputies are not trained to handle psychiatric crises — and that the county has nowhere to send people who need real care. Deputies are constantly pulled off patrol for mental-health calls, he said, then left to put those in crisis in hotels because there aren't enough hospital beds available.

"Additionally, we really struggle when we have people in custody who we aren't equipped to handle, and secure beds are even harder to find," Kusminsky said. "It sometimes takes weeks or months to locate once and when we do, they are maybe on the other side of the state and at an exorbitant cost."

"Hotels and motels don’t have doctors, don’t have medicine, don’t have therapy," Komatireddy said. "The state needs to step in."

For at least one night, WWE’s Saturday Night’s Main Event will transform into Sunday Night’s Main Event as the showcase will take place in Atlanta on Labor Day weekend.
